INT type mapping is appropriate for both ProductID and NewQuantity
Parameter names prefixed with 'p_' to follow PostgreSQL naming conventions
SET NOCOUNT ON behavior is not required as PostgreSQL procedures don't return row counts to clients by default

No transaction control is needed as the single UPDATE statement is atomic

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server UPDATE statements acquire row locks by default. PostgreSQL also locks rows during UPDATE, but the specific locking semantics may differ. If the procedure name implies specific locking requirements, explicit FOR UPDATE locks may be needed in a SELECT before the UPDATE.

SQL Server default isolation level is READ COMMITTED with row versioning (depending on configuration). PostgreSQL default is also READ COMMITTED but uses MVCC. Concurrent behavior may differ slightly under high contention.

SQL Server procedures implicitly return 0 on success or error codes. PostgreSQL procedures (as of PG 11+) do not return values. If the calling application expects a return code, consider converting to a FUNCTION returning INTEGER or using OUT parameters.
PostgreSQL procedures do not send row count messages to clients by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON behavior is implicit and requires no conversion.
